## Summary

Write this last. Three to five sentences: the problem, who has it in Greece, what they use today, and whether this item looks worth pursuing.

## The problem

What job is the person trying to get done? Describe it in plain words, as if to someone outside shipping. Name the documents and data involved (for example: noon report, SOF, charter party).

## Who has it in Greece

- Roles: which person in which company feels the pain (owner, technical manager, operations manager, chartering desk, accounts).
- Company types: owner, manager, operator, broker, charterer.
- Company size: number of ships.
- How many Greek companies fit this, with the source.

## Who pays

- Who signs off on buying a tool for this.
- What they spend today: staff time, an outsourced service, or software.
- Any sign of willingness to pay.

## What they use today

Excel, email, an ERP module, an outsourced service, or nothing. Say where each claim comes from.

## Rules and standards

Regulations, industry forms (for example BIMCO clauses) and data standards that shape this item. Include dates that change the market.

## Size of the opportunity

A rough estimate with its method shown. For example: number of Greek companies × likely price per ship × ships per company. Mark it as a guess if it is one.
